title: Subsidies for Private Speech and Occupational Therapy Sessions for Autistic Children
what_it_is: Subsidies for Private Speech and Occupational Therapy Sessions for Autistic Children

sections.label: ECDA funding and fee caps
sections.summary: ECDA funds EIPIC and EIPIC-P, with means-tested fee caps; a median income family pays up to $210 or $360 monthly.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Goh Pei Ming) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
sentences.text: The Early Childhood Development Agency (ECDA) funds both Early Intervention Programme for Infants and Children (EIPIC), delivered by social service agencies, and EIPIC-P, delivered by appointed private providers.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Goh Pei Ming) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
sentences.text: Means-tested fee caps are established to ensure that operators provide quality services at an affordable fee.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Goh Pei Ming) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
sentences.text: A median income family pays up to $210 a month for EIPIC and $360 a month for EIPIC-P.

sections.label: Intervention hours and CDA use
sections.summary: Enrolled children get five to 12 hours of intervention weekly, and parents may use CDA funds for registered supplementary early intervention services.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Goh Pei Ming) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
sentences.text: Enrolled children typically receive five to 12 hours of intervention conducted over two or three sessions every week, with the frequency and duration of the sessions tailored according to the level of support the child needs.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Goh Pei Ming) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
sentences.text: Parents who wish to seek supplementary intervention beyond those provided under EIPIC or EIPIC-P may also tap on the Child Development Account (CDA) to pay for additional early intervention services by early intervention providers registered with ECDA.

sections.label: ECDA-registered private providers
sections.summary: ECDA strongly recommends parents use ECDA-registered service providers, which is how the Government regulates services and controls costs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
sentences.text: First, in terms of private providers, from ECDA's perspective, we strongly recommend that parents go with the list of service providers registered with ECDA.

sentences.speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
sentences.text: This is also the Government's way of regulating services and controlling costs.

sections.label: CDA funds for extra sessions
sections.summary: Parents choosing additional sessions beyond what professionals consider cardinal can use CDA account funds to pay for them.

sentences.speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
sentences.text: Sometimes, parents may choose to do even more, but that is not what the professionals would say are cardinal.

sentences.speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
sentences.text: Therefore, if parents choose to use additional sessions, they can use the CDA account funds to pay for those.
